name: Destiny

income.note: Effective tax rate ~18% including federal + GA state income tax (5.49%). PSLF eligible after 10 years — a meaningful but distant financial lever.

monthly_expenses_breakdown.student_loan_note: On Income-Driven Repayment (IDR) plan. Actual payment is $98/mo vs standard repayment of $380/mo. Pursuing PSLF — 10-year forgiveness if she stays in nonprofit.

monthly_surplus_note: Surplus looks reasonable on paper but is inconsistent month-to-month. Unexpected expenses (medical, car repair, travel) regularly wipe it out. 59% of Americans cannot cover a $1,000 unexpected expense (Bankrate 2025) — Destiny is in this group.

savings_breakdown.note: Nonprofit employer offers 403(b) but Destiny has not enrolled — couldn't afford contributions when she started. Just opened a HYSA 4 months ago. Emergency fund goal is $9,800 (3 months). Currently at 12% of goal. 55% of Gen Z do not have enough emergency savings to cover 3 months (multiple sources, 2025).

debt_breakdown.student_loan_note: Social sciences / public policy bachelor's degree. EducationData avg for behavioral sciences: $44,554. Destiny's balance is slightly below avg. On IDR + PSLF track — psychologically reduces urgency but delays actual payoff.
debt_breakdown.credit_card_note: Below Millennial avg of $6,961 — Destiny avoids credit cards after a bad experience at 22. Has one card used only for emergencies.
debt_breakdown.bnpl_note: 44% of Gen Z used BNPL in 2024 (Motley Fool). Destiny has 2 active Afterpay plans (clothing, $480) and 1 Affirm plan (phone accessories, $1,320). 25% of Gen Z were late on a BNPL payment in 2024 — Destiny missed one payment in the last 6 months.
debt_breakdown.medical_debt_note: ER visit (appendix scare) at 23 while uninsured between jobs. 18% of adults 18-29 have borrowed money for healthcare (Federal Reserve SHED 2024). Paying $80/mo on a payment plan.

financial_goals: Build $2,500 emergency fund in next 8 months (first milestone)
Clear all BNPL obligations within 4 months
Enroll in 403(b) at 3% contribution by end of year
Pay off medical debt by month 14
Qualify for PSLF student loan forgiveness in 7.5 years
subscriptions_detail: Amazon Prime shared with family ($0 her share)
subscription_note: Notably lean — Destiny audited her subscriptions 3 months ago after a viral TikTok about 'subscription creep.' Cut 4 services. This is a sign of growing financial awareness.

behavioral_profile.money_script: I grew up without much money and I'm afraid I'll always be bad at this — but I'm trying to change that.
spending_triggers: Stress-spending after a hard day ('I deserve something small')
30% of Gen Z treat themselves to purchases when worried about money (Fortune 2024) — Destiny fits this
Social media: TikTok Shop and Instagram ads are primary triggers — 9 in 10 Gen Z impulse buy on social media (GoDaddy 2024)
BNPL availability removes friction — installments feel 'manageable' in the moment
Seeing friends or coworkers with new items creates social pull
'Doom spending' when news cycle is heavy — documented Gen Z coping pattern (Fortune 2024)
cognitive_biases_observed: Present bias: IDR loan plan reduces monthly pain but delays financial progress
BNPL optimism: consistently underestimates how quickly BNPL balances accumulate
Scarcity mindset flip: occasional 'treat yourself' overspending as psychological release from chronic financial constraint
Avoidance: 33% of Gen Z avoid thinking about finances when stressed (research, 2024) — Destiny has periods of this
shopping_patterns: Primarily shops via TikTok Shop, Instagram, Shein, and ASOS
Impulse purchase window is very short — often buys within minutes of seeing a product
Uses BNPL to make purchases feel affordable
Nearly half of Gen Z put themselves on 'shopping bans' then break them (retail research 2024) — Destiny has done this twice
behavioral_profile.financial_anxiety_notes: 48% of Gen Z financially insecure in 2025 — up 60% from 2024 (Deloitte). 62% of Gen Z stressed 3+ days/week about money (LifeStance 2025). Destiny has high anxiety but is actively rebuilding — this is the key narrative tension. She is making real progress (HYSA opened, subscriptions audited, IDR enrolled) but one unexpected expense can set her back months.
behavioral_profile.financial_identity_note: Destiny is actively trying to shift her self-concept from 'bad with money' to 'someone who is learning.' This is fragile and should be affirmed — not undermined. Non-judgmental framing is critical.

demo_context.coaching_note: Destiny's $834 surplus looks adequate but her BNPL balance is still active and emergency fund is critically low. The sneakers are likely a stress-triggered social media impulse. Coach should validate the desire, name the BNPL pattern gently, and redirect to her savings milestone.
